---
title: "RStudio IDE"
subtitle: "Panes, source editor, projects, version control, debugging, and keyboard shortcuts"
---

RStudio is an integrated development environment (IDE) for R. It wraps the R
console in four main panes — Source, Console, Environment/History, and
Files/Plots/Packages/Help — plus tools for projects, version control,
package development, and debugging.

::: {.source-note}
📄 Based on the RStudio IDE cheatsheet, RStudio 2026.07.1
:::

## The four panes

By default RStudio arranges its panes in a 2×2 grid. Drag pane boundaries to
resize, or use the maximize/minimize icons on each pane's toolbar.

::: {.fn-ref}
`Source Editor`
: Where you write and edit scripts (`.R`), R Markdown/Quarto documents, Shiny apps, and more. Includes syntax highlighting, tab completion, code diagnostics, multi-cursor editing (`Alt/Option + drag`), and a file outline for jumping to functions or sections.

`Console / Terminal / Jobs`
: Run R code interactively in the Console, use the Terminal tab for shell commands, and run long scripts in the background with Jobs so your console stays free.

`Environment / History / Connections`
: Environment lists your saved objects by type, with tools to load/save the workspace and clear it. History shows past commands you can re-run or copy. Connections manages external databases.

`Files / Plots / Packages / Help / Viewer`
: Files is a browser keyed to your working directory. Plots shows a history of your graphics. Packages lists and manages installed packages. Help displays documentation. Viewer renders HTML content like Shiny apps and R Markdown/Quarto output.
:::

## Documents and apps

RStudio recognizes file types and opens them with the right tools automatically.

| File / project type | What RStudio gives you |
|---|---|
| R scripts (`.R`) | Run selected code, re-run previous code, source with/without echo, or as a local job. |
| R Markdown / Quarto (`.Rmd`, `.qmd`) | Knit/render button, chunk execution controls, spell check, and a Visual Editor for WYSIWYG markdown editing. |
| Shiny apps (`app.R`, or `ui.R` + `server.R` + `global.R`) | A **Run App** button, a chooser for where to view the app (window, viewer pane, or browser), and one-click publishing to shinyapps.io or Posit Connect. |
| R packages | A Build pane with Install & Restart, `devtools::load_all()`, `R CMD check`, and package tests, plus Roxygen-based documentation. |

::: {.callout-tip}
The **Visual Editor** for R Markdown/Quarto behaves like a word processor: format text, insert tables, citations, and equations, and it stays in sync with the underlying markdown source.
:::

## Projects

Create a project with `File > New Project`. RStudio saves the call history,
workspace, and working directory associated with a project and reloads them
each time you reopen it — this keeps unrelated analyses cleanly separated.
Projects can also be shared with collaborators, run in multiple simultaneous
R sessions, and switched between different R versions.

## Version control (Git)

Turn on Git integration at `Tools > Project Options > Git/SVN`. The Git pane
shows file status at a glance and lets you stage, commit, and push/pull
without leaving RStudio.

| Status letter | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **A** | Added |
| **D** | Deleted |
| **M** | Modified |
| **R** | Renamed |
| **?** | Untracked |

Stage files, commit with a message, view file diffs, browse commit history,
and push/pull to a remote — all from the Git pane toolbar. An embedded shell
is also available for anything not covered by the GUI.

## Package development

Start a new package with `File > New Project > New Directory > R Package`,
then enable Roxygen documentation at `Tools > Project Options > Build Tools`.
The Build pane gives you:

::: {.fn-ref}
`devtools::load_all()`
: Reload the package's changed code without a full install — the fastest development loop.

`Install and Restart`
: Install the package and restart R with it freshly loaded.

`Run R CMD check`
: Run the standard CRAN-style package checks for structural and documentation issues.

`Run package tests`
: Execute your test suite (e.g. testthat) from the Build pane.
:::

## Debug mode

Trigger the debugger with `debug()`, `browser()`, or by clicking next to a
line number to set a breakpoint, then execute your code. While paused,
RStudio highlights the current line and gives you:

- **Step controls** — step through code one line at a time, or step into/out of functions.
- **Environment inspection** — examine variables in the currently executing environment.
- **Console access** — run commands directly in the paused environment.
- **Traceback** — open the traceback to see the sequence of function calls that led to an error, and jump the debugger to its origin.

## Posit Assistant

Posit Assistant is a built-in data analysis assistant that connects to your
live R and Python sessions. It can see your data and help you explore,
visualize, build, and debug — with a mode selector (Normal, Plan, Auto,
Cleaning), slash commands, web search, and the ability to reference
workspace files with `@`.

## Essential keyboard shortcuts

| Action | Windows / Linux | Mac |
|---|---|---|
| Search command history | `Ctrl + ↑` | `Cmd + ↑` |
| Interrupt current command | `Esc` | `Esc` |
| Clear console | `Ctrl + L` | `Ctrl + L` |
| Go to File/Function | `Ctrl + .` | `Ctrl + .` |
| Attempt completion | `Tab` / `Ctrl+Space` | `Tab` / `Ctrl+Space` |
| Insert `<-` | `Alt + -` | `Option + -` |
| Insert `\|>` pipe | `Ctrl+Shift+M` | `Cmd+Shift+M` |
| (Un)Comment selection | `Ctrl+Shift+C` | `Cmd+Shift+C` |
| Knit/Render document | `Ctrl+Shift+K` | `Cmd+Shift+K` |
| Load all (devtools) | `Ctrl+Shift+L` | `Cmd+Shift+L` |
| Test package | `Ctrl+Shift+T` | `Cmd+Shift+T` |
| Document package | `Ctrl+Shift+D` | `Cmd+Shift+D` |
| Show Command Palette | `Ctrl+Shift+P` | `Cmd+Shift+P` |
| Keyboard Shortcuts Help | `Alt+Shift+K` | `Option+Shift+K` |

::: {.callout-note}
Can't remember a shortcut? Open the Command Palette (`Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+P`) and search by name, or view the full quick reference with `Tools > Keyboard Shortcuts`.
:::
